**6. SAFETY PROTOCOLS AND UNION RULES**

All crew members must be current members of IATSE Local 399. This includes all
department heads, day players, and freelancers. Proof of membership must be presented

membership will not be permitted to work. No exceptions will be made.

**Safety Orientation**

A mandatory safety orientation will be held on 08-28-2026 at 08:00 at the Harbor Lot
before equipment prep begins. Attendance is required for all crew members, including
day players who are scheduled for any date during principal photography. The
orientation will cover:

- Location-specific hazards at Harbor Lot, Soundstage B, and Riverfront Exteriors
- Proper lifting and carrying techniques
- Fire safety and evacuation routes for each location
- Weather procedures, including heat and rain protocols
- Emergency contact procedures (see Section 7)

**Personal Protective Equipment**

All crew members are required to wear closed-toe shoes with non-slip soles at all
times on set. Safety glasses must be worn during any rigging or striking operation.
Hard hats are required in the Harbor Lot equipment staging area and during any
overhead work. Grip and Electric crew will be issued additional PPE as needed;
contact Marcus Boone or Priya Natarajan if you need replacement equipment.

**Studio and Location Rules**

- Smoking is permitted only in designated areas. No smoking on any interior set or
  within 25 feet of any exterior set.
- No open flames on set without the approval of the Key Grip and the Set Medic.
- All weapons and props that resemble weapons must be checked in and out with the
  Property Master each day. No live ammunition is permitted on set at any time.
- Food and drink are not permitted on any set or on any standing set piece. Catering
  is available in the designated craft services area.
- All cables and wiring must be taped down or otherwise protected. Grip and Electric
  are responsible for ensuring that all walkways remain clear.

3.4 Caterer shall provide a minimum of two (2) menu choices at the main entree station at each meal period, one of which shall be a protein-based dish and one of which shall be a plant-based dish. Salads, bread, and beverages shall be available at each meal service.

**VENDOR CONTRACTS – THE LAST FERRY**

**Agreement No. 2026-014 (General Terms and Conditions)**
**Effective Date: January 15, 2026**
**Last Amended: October 30, 2026**

This document sets forth the standard terms and conditions applicable to all vendor agreements entered into by Last Ferry Productions, LLC (hereafter "Production") with external vendors providing goods or services in connection with the production of the motion picture currently titled "The Last Ferry." These general terms are incorporated by reference into each individual Statement of Work, Purchase Order, or Service Agreement executed with Production. In the event of a conflict between these General Terms and the specific terms of an individual agreement, the specific terms shall control.

---

**1. DEFINITIONS.**

1.1 "Vendor" means the party providing goods or services to Production under an individual agreement incorporating these terms.

1.2 "Deliverables" means all goods, services, materials, data, and intellectual property to be provided by Vendor under an individual agreement.

1.3 "Work" means all activities performed by Vendor in connection with the Deliverables.

1.4 "Confidential Information" means any non-public information disclosed by one party to the other, including but not limited to: script materials, production schedules, budgets, cast and crew lists, footage, technical specifications, and business strategies.

---

**2. PAYMENT TERMS.**

2.1 **Invoicing.** Vendor shall submit invoices in accordance with the schedule set forth in the individual agreement. Each invoice must reference the applicable Agreement Number and, where applicable, the relevant Purchase Order number. Invoices lacking required references may be returned for correction and shall not be deemed received until properly resubmitted.

2.2 **Payment Schedule.** Unless otherwise stated in an individual agreement, Production shall pay undisputed amounts within thirty (30) days of receipt of a complete and accurate invoice. Payment shall be made by check or electronic funds transfer, at Production's discretion.

2.3 **Disputed Amounts.** If Production disputes any portion of an invoice, Production shall pay the undisputed portion within the time specified in Section 2.2 and shall provide written notice of the disputed amount, with reasonable detail, within fifteen (15) business days of receipt of the invoice. The parties shall work in good faith to resolve any dispute promptly.

2.4 **Taxes.** Vendor shall be responsible for all applicable federal, state, and local taxes arising from its performance of the Work, including but not limited to income, payroll, and self-employment taxes. Production shall not be responsible for any taxes owed by Vendor, except as required by law.

2.5 **No Set-Off.** Unless otherwise agreed in writing, Vendor shall not set off or withhold any amounts due to Production against amounts owed to Vendor.

---

**3. INSURANCE REQUIREMENTS.**

3.1 **General Requirements.** Vendor shall, at its sole cost and expense, procure and maintain the insurance coverage described in this Section 3. Such insurance shall be placed with insurers rated A- or better by A.M. Best Company and shall be primary and non-contributory to any insurance maintained by Production.

3.2 **Workers' Compensation.** Vendor shall maintain Workers' Compensation insurance in accordance with the statutory requirements of the state(s) in which the Work is performed, and Employer's Liability insurance with limits of at least One Million Dollars ($1,000,000) per accident, per disease, and per employee.

3.3 **Commercial General Liability.** Vendor shall maintain Commercial General Liability insurance on an occurrence basis, including products and completed operations coverage, with limits of not less than Two Million Dollars ($2,000,000) per occurrence and Two Million Dollars ($2,000,000) in the aggregate.

3.4 **Automobile Liability.** If Vendor uses any vehicles in connection with the Work, Vendor shall maintain Automobile Liability insurance covering all owned, hired, and non-owned vehicles with a combined single limit of not less than One Million Dollars ($1,000,000) per accident.
